title: Recent Inflation Developments and Challenges for Research and Monetary Policymaking
summary: Loretta Mester, former President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland, delivered this speech in May 2016 discussing inflation dynamics and the challenges of achieving the Fed's 2% PCE inflation target. The speech reviews low inflation conditions across the US, UK, and Euro area in 2015, citing weak global demand, energy/commodity price declines, and dollar strength as contributing factors. The speech is explicitly framed as her own views rather than official FOMC policy signals.
key_points: Fed adopted explicit 2% PCE inflation target in January 2012, described as symmetric (Committee concerned about persistent deviations in either direction)
Historical inflation misses cited: deflation during Great Depression (1930s) and high inflation following 1970s oil shocks before Volcker's tightening
2015 inflation readings: UK 0.20% (CPI), Euro area 0.25% (HICP), US 0.66% (PCE) — all well below respective targets
SIGMA model estimates: 10% real dollar appreciation reduces core inflation by ~0.5% after one year via import prices
Three common factors driving low inflation: weak global demand post-crisis, falling energy/commodity prices, dollar appreciation
Speech represents author's personal views, explicitly noted as not necessarily those of FOMC colleagues
why_it_matters: This speech provides historical context on the post-Great Recession low inflation environment and the Fed's framework for understanding inflation determinants. While not providing current policy signals, it illustrates the Fed's analytical tools (SIGMA model) for assessing dollar and commodity price pass-through to inflation. Relevant for understanding the intellectual framework behind FOMC inflation assessments during this period.
macro_context: The speech addresses macro conditions circa 2015-2016: persistent below-target inflation across major central banks, weak global demand, and dollar appreciation effects. The SIGMA model quantification of exchange rate pass-through (0.5% core inflation impact per 10% dollar move) provides analytical framework. Speech emphasizes uncertainty in inflation forecasting and need for ongoing research.
important_numbers: 0.5% (estimated core inflation drop per 10% dollar appreciation per SIGMA model)
notes: Historical speech from 2016 by former Cleveland Fed President Loretta Mester. While containing relevant content on inflation dynamics and Fed frameworks, the source is stale (~10 years old) and provides no current policy signals. Classified as speech_neutral as it discusses inflation research challenges rather than signaling directional policy intent. Useful as historical archive for understanding Fed's analytical approach during the low-inflation post-crisis period but not actionable for current macro catalyst assessment.
